programme.title: Scotland's Home of the Year
programme.desc: The judges head east where they must choose between a colourful villa in Fife, a new build overlooking the Firth of Forth and a mid-century bungalow in Linlithgow.

programme.title: Island Crossings
programme.desc: As overhaul season continues, captain Andy Gill explains the extended dry dock period that is delaying one of Arran's main passenger and freight vessels beyond its planned two-week overhaul schedule, causing havoc with the rest of the network.

programme.title: Black Black Oil
programme.desc: North Sea oil has been an invisible machine at the core of the UK. It now faces an uncertain future as activists and investors demand change. Oil companies are convinced that they can continue to keep drilling while keeping to net-zero ambitions through adopting new technologies, such as carbon capture. But climate scientists are deeply sceptical of the net-zero concept and the time it would take for these technologies to be effective.

programme.title: River City
programme.desc: Things take a terrifying turn when Tommy collapses after being diagnosed with concussion. A dejected Tyler is forced to contemplate his next moves with Harry. Amber's attempts at a grand gesture to Angus are interrupted by Teddy.

programme.title: Icons of Football
programme.desc: A portrait of legendary former Scotland captain Gary McAllister, a classy midfielder who suffered heartbreaking lows as well as highs that stand as a testament to his enduring class.

programme.title: Scotcast
programme.desc: Martin Geissler hears how extreme weather has prompted scientists and farmers to re-think how we produce enough food.

programme.title: The Trials That Shocked Scotland
programme.desc: A look at a family's 18-year fight for justice following the 1998 murder of Surjit Singh Chhokar in Overtown. There is also the 2015 trial of William Paterson at the High Court in Glasgow. Paterson stood accused of shooting to death a well-known gangland figure in a busy supermarket car park five years earlier.

programme.title: Hidden Lives
programme.desc: Vonny LeClerc delves into the fast and furious world of roller derby. The sport has exploded in popularity over the past decade with teams springing up all over Scotland. A cross between British bulldog and speed skating, it demands fitness, technique and skating skills, but in exchange for dedication there is an unrivalled feeling of community. Rediscovering her own passion for the sport, Vonny visits her old team in Edinburgh, the Auld Reekie Roller Girls.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: George Anderson and Brian Cunningham delve into the mailbox to tackle a host of viewers' questions sent in from around the country.

programme.title: Scotland's Greatest Escape
programme.desc: It's wildcard week, where we visit three escapes that don't fit into any of this year's categories but that our industry panel decided had to be included. Kirsty and Helen from Perthshire rate former farm Monachyle Mhor in the Trossachs, House of Gods hotel in Edinburgh, and Glen Dye, a 15,000-acre private estate in Aberdeenshire.

programme.title: Martin Compston's Scottish Fling
programme.desc: Martin Compston and good friend Phil MacHugh travel up the west coast of Scotland 'through villages and towns' on an adventure to discover the different ways people experience the great Scottish outdoors. Their journey begins in Martin's hometown of Greenock, where Phil has arranged some unexpected transport across the water to sunny Dunoon. Next, the boys pick up their campervan Celine and head to the banks of Loch Lomond to meet Instagram rambler the Hillwalking Hijabi, Zahrah Mahmood.

programme.title: Martin Compston's Scottish Fling
programme.desc: Martin is given a taste of island life when pal Phil takes him on a journey to his family's homeland of the Western Isles. From an unexpected Hebridean pipe-playing welcome at the airport in Stornoway, Martin and Phil embark on their island odyssey.

programme.title: Scot Squad
programme.desc: Newly promoted PC Ken Beattie finds himself called upon to provide a character reference. Singh and McKirdy gallantly help out a hen do, and the Chief attempts international diplomacy by shouting loudly at a laptop.

programme.title: Edinburgh Unlocked
programme.desc: Mark Nelson and his all-star team of reporters present the best, funniest, wildest and weirdest shows from the Edinburgh Festival.

programme.title: Scotcast
programme.desc: Conversation about Scotland's biggest news stories, hosted by Martin Geissler.

programme.title: Growing Up Scottish
programme.desc: Some of Scotland's comedians and entertainers go on journey through friendships past, reminiscing on the bonding, the hanging out, the best friends, the sleepovers and the strange noises.
